paragraphs.source_en: The master's wife had pushed the nursing baby more than a foot away; her mouth was open as she snored, and her head had slipped from the pillow. In my opinion, among all the unsightly things about human beings, nothing is more improper than sleeping with one's mouth open. We cats have never disgraced ourselves like that in all our lives. Originally the mouth is for making sounds, and the nose is the organ for drawing in and sending out air. To be sure, up north people grow lazy, open their mouths as little as possible, and end by speaking through the nose, so that their speech is always a sort of droning twang. But to shut up the nose and make the mouth alone perform the task of breathing is even more unseemly than that twang. For one thing, if mouse droppings were to fall from the ceiling, how dangerous it would be.

paragraphs.source_en: I next looked at the children's sleeping forms; they were no less ridiculous than their parents, sprawled face down in deep sleep. The elder sister, Tonko, as though displaying the authority of elder sisterhood, had stretched her right arm straight out and laid it over her younger sister's ear. The younger sister, Sunko, in revenge, had raised one leg in lordly fashion and placed it on her sister's belly; both of them had turned a full ninety degrees from the positions in which they had originally lain down. What was most remarkable was that, maintaining these unnatural postures all the while, both girls slept soundly without the least complaint.

paragraphs.source_en: Indeed, lamplight on a spring night has a charm all its own. Behind this scene, innocent and yet utterly devoid of elegance, the lamp shone with a quiet grace, as if admonishing one to cherish the lovely night. I wondered what time it could be now. I looked around the room: the neighborhood was still, and all I could hear was the ticking of the wall clock, the mistress's snoring, and, far off, the maidservant grinding her teeth. Whenever people tell this maidservant that she grinds her teeth in her sleep, she flatly denies it. She stubbornly insists, "From the day I was born until now, I have no recollection of ever grinding my teeth." She never says, "I shall certainly mend my ways," or "I am sorry to have disturbed you"; she simply maintains, "I have no recollection of ever grinding my teeth." Of course, since it is a skill she performs in her sleep, she surely cannot remember it. Still, though she herself may not remember it, the fact remains; there is simply no helping her. There are people in the world who plainly do bad things while all the while considering themselves good people. Since such a person is confident of his own innocence, he is naturally carefree and at ease, and there is nothing more to be said. Yet however carefree he may be, that cannot erase the fact that he causes trouble for others. Ladies and gentlemen of this sort are probably of the same breed as this maidservant. The night was already far advanced.

units.source_en: Indeed, lamplight on a spring night has a charm all its own.

paragraphs.source_zh: 果然春宵的灯火是别有一番情趣的。在这种天真烂漫同时又是极端缺乏风流的光景背后，灯火放出雅静的光辉仿佛在告诫人们要爱惜这个良宵。我心想，现在是什么时刻了呢？便环视了一下室内，四邻寂寂，听到的只是挂钟的滴嗒声、女主人的鼾声和远处女佣人的错牙声。当人们说这个女佣人睡觉错牙时，她总要矢口否认。她总是顽固地坚持说：“从我生下来直到今天，我不记得错过牙呀。”她决不说“我一定改正”或“吵你们啦”，只是坚决主张“我不记得错过牙呀”。当然，这是她睡梦中的本事，肯定她是不会记得的。不过，本人虽不记得，而事实毕竟存在，真是拿她没办法。世上有的人明明做坏事，而他本人却始终自认为好人。他既然自信自己无罪，自然就很轻松自在，没什么可说的。不过，不管他本人怎样轻松自在，却抹杀不了给别人带来祸害这一事实。像这类的绅士淑女大概就是和这个女佣人属于同一类型的吧。夜已经很深了。

paragraphs.source_en: Someone tapped lightly twice on the kitchen storm shutter. How strange: who could be coming at this hour of the night? It was probably those mice at their mischief again. If it was a mouse, I had in any case resolved not to catch it, so it could make whatever trouble it pleased. Again came two thumps: ton, ton. It did not seem like a mouse; if it was one, then it was an exceedingly cautious mouse. The mice in the master's house, like the students at the school where he teaches, are a lot who spend day and night devising acts of disorder and violence, and who regard startling the poor master from pleasant dreams as their appointed vocation; naturally they would never be so polite as this. The visitor just now was certainly not a mouse. If it were the mouse that recently invaded the master's bedroom, bit the tip of his low nose, and withdrew in triumph, it would never be this careful. This was no mouse; while I was thinking so, I heard the shutter being pushed upward from below. Then came the sound of the paper door by the corridor being slid open as slowly as possible; this made it still less likely to be a mouse. It was a human being! If, at this depth of night, a person should break in without so much as calling from outside and condescend to pay us a visit, it could certainly be neither Mr. Meitei nor Mr. Suzuki. Could it be, then, the gentleman of the rafters whose great name I had already heard? If it was indeed such a burglar-gentleman, how eager I was to make his acquaintance at once. This gentleman of the rafters was now raising his great muddy feet and coming into the kitchen, and seemed to have taken two steps forward. Probably on what must have been his third step, he caught his foot on the loose kitchen floorboard, and a heavy thud rang through the silent night. The hair on my back stood up as though it had been brushed the wrong way with a shoe brush. For a good while there was no sound of footsteps at all. I looked at the master's wife; she still had her mouth open and was inhaling and exhaling the peaceful air in her dreams. As for the master, he was dreaming sweetly with his thumb caught in a red-covered book. Before long, the sound of a match being struck came from the kitchen. It seemed that this gentleman of the rafters did not see as well in the dark as we do. Unable to make out the state of the room, he must have found it highly inconvenient.

units.source_en: Someone tapped lightly twice on the kitchen storm shutter. How strange: who could be coming at this hour of the night?
units.source_zh: 有人轻轻地敲了两下厨房的防雨板，真怪呀，深更半夜怎么会有人来呢？

units.source_en: It was probably those mice at their mischief again.
units.source_zh: 大概又是老鼠在作怪吧。

units.source_en: If it was a mouse, I had in any case resolved not to catch it, so it could make whatever trouble it pleased.
units.source_zh: 如果是老鼠，反正我是决心不去捕捉的，随你去折腾吧。

units.source_en: Again came two thumps: ton, ton.
units.source_zh: 又是咚咚的两响。

units.source_en: It did not seem like a mouse; if it was one, then it was an exceedingly cautious mouse.
units.source_zh: 看来不像是老鼠，假如是老鼠，那也是个警惕性很高的老鼠。

units.source_en: The mice in the master's house, like the students at the school where he teaches, are a lot who spend day and night devising acts of disorder and violence, and who regard startling the poor master from pleasant dreams as their appointed vocation; naturally they would never be so polite as this.
units.source_zh: 主人家的那些老鼠，都是一些像主人教书的那个学校里的学生一样，不管白天黑夜总是用尽心思去琢磨怎样捣乱，把惊破可怜的主人的好梦作为它们天职的一群家伙，所以自然不会这样客客气气的。

units.source_en: The visitor just now was certainly not a mouse.
units.source_zh: 现在来的肯定不是老鼠。

units.source_en: If it were the mouse that recently invaded the master's bedroom, bit the tip of his low nose, and withdrew in triumph, it would never be this careful.
units.source_zh: 如果是前些日子闯入主人卧室咬了主人那低低的鼻头，然后凯旋归去的那只老鼠，是不会这样小心翼翼的。

units.source_en: This was no mouse; while I was thinking so, I heard the shutter being pushed upward from below.
units.source_zh: 这决不是老鼠，我正寻思着，又听到把防雨板从下往上拍的声音。

units.source_en: Then came the sound of the paper door by the corridor being slid open as slowly as possible; this made it still less likely to be a mouse.
units.source_zh: 然后是把廊内纸门尽量缓缓推开的声音，这更加不会是老鼠了。

units.source_en: It was a human being!
units.source_zh: 是个人！

units.source_en: If, at this depth of night, a person should break in without so much as calling from outside and condescend to pay us a visit, it could certainly be neither Mr. Meitei nor Mr. Suzuki.
units.source_zh: 在这样的深更半夜，一个人居然不在门外招呼一声就破门而入，屈尊光临，肯定不会是迷亭先生或铃木君。

units.source_en: Could it be, then, the gentleman of the rafters whose great name I had already heard?
units.source_zh: 那么是不是我早已听到过大名的梁上君子呢？

units.source_en: If it was indeed such a burglar-gentleman, how eager I was to make his acquaintance at once.
units.source_zh: 如果是梁上君子，我是多么想尽早拜识他啊。

units.source_en: This gentleman of the rafters was now raising his great muddy feet and coming into the kitchen, and seemed to have taken two steps forward.
units.source_zh: 这位梁上君子现在抬起他的大泥脚正走到厨房里来，而且好像是往前迈了两步。

units.source_en: Probably on what must have been his third step, he caught his foot on the loose kitchen floorboard, and a heavy thud rang through the silent night.
units.source_zh: 大概是他在迈第三步的时候，可能绊在厨房的活动地板上了吧，发出了咕咚一声冲破了静夜。

units.source_en: The hair on my back stood up as though it had been brushed the wrong way with a shoe brush.
units.source_zh: 我感到脊背上的毛就像用鞋刷子给戗着擦过似的倒竖起来。

units.source_en: For a good while there was no sound of footsteps at all.
units.source_zh: 好一阵子再也听不到任何脚步声了。

units.source_en: I looked at the master's wife; she still had her mouth open and was inhaling and exhaling the peaceful air in her dreams.
units.source_zh: 我看了看主人的妻子，她仍张着嘴在梦中吞吐着太平空气。

units.source_en: As for the master, he was dreaming sweetly with his thumb caught in a red-covered book.
units.source_zh: 而主人呢，则把一本红皮书捏在拇指间，正做美梦哩。

units.source_en: Before long, the sound of a match being struck came from the kitchen.
units.source_zh: 不久，厨房里传来了划火柴的声音。

units.source_en: It seemed that this gentleman of the rafters did not see as well in the dark as we do.
units.source_zh: 看来，这位梁上君子在夜里目力不像我辈那么管用。

units.source_en: Unable to make out the state of the room, he must have found it highly inconvenient.
units.source_zh: 他摸不清室内的情况，肯定是不太方便的。

paragraphs.source_zh: 有人轻轻地敲了两下厨房的防雨板，真怪呀，深更半夜怎么会有人来呢？大概又是老鼠在作怪吧。如果是老鼠，反正我是决心不去捕捉的，随你去折腾吧。又是咚咚的两响。看来不像是老鼠，假如是老鼠，那也是个警惕性很高的老鼠。主人家的那些老鼠，都是一些像主人教书的那个学校里的学生一样，不管白天黑夜总是用尽心思去琢磨怎样捣乱，把惊破可怜的主人的好梦作为它们天职的一群家伙，所以自然不会这样客客气气的。现在来的肯定不是老鼠。如果是前些日子闯入主人卧室咬了主人那低低的鼻头，然后凯旋归去的那只老鼠，是不会这样小心翼翼的。这决不是老鼠，我正寻思着，又听到把防雨板从下往上拍的声音。然后是把廊内纸门尽量缓缓推开的声音，这更加不会是老鼠了。是个人！在这样的深更半夜，一个人居然不在门外招呼一声就破门而入，屈尊光临，肯定不会是迷亭先生或铃木君。那么是不是我早已听到过大名的梁上君子呢？如果是梁上君子，我是多么想尽早拜识他啊。这位梁上君子现在抬起他的大泥脚正走到厨房里来，而且好像是往前迈了两步。大概是他在迈第三步的时候，可能绊在厨房的活动地板上了吧，发出了咕咚一声冲破了静夜。我感到脊背上的毛就像用鞋刷子给戗着擦过似的倒竖起来。好一阵子再也听不到任何脚步声了。我看了看主人的妻子，她仍张着嘴在梦中吞吐着太平空气。而主人呢，则把一本红皮书捏在拇指间，正做美梦哩。不久，厨房里传来了划火柴的声音。看来，这位梁上君子在夜里目力不像我辈那么管用。他摸不清室内的情况，肯定是不太方便的。
